findings.reason: without its own measure the wiring node cannot be closed or falsified, and the section's current Done-when will be satisfied by re-running a test that already passes, closing §9 with the producer still off the fleet node.
findings.text: §9 declares a second node ("A second node calls the decision from the producer: its write paths are `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py` (start-up, in `_watch_registration`), `reckon/crew/runs.py` (lease renewal), `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py` and its test") but the section's only Done-when at :305 is already satisfied at HEAD: `watch_unit.producer_start_decision` (`watch_unit.py:246`) landed in `552f75681` (2026-10-23 17:27 +0200) with all four arms of that Done-when in `tests/test_a_producer_off_the_fleet_node_gives_up_its_seat.py` (release-and-exit, unit-disable composed, same-host hold, absent-record hold, real-record-untouched), and nothing outside that test calls the decision (`grep -rn producer_start_decision` returns only the definition and the test), so the wiring node — the half that makes the decision run on the real code path — has neither a measurable done-when nor a declared negative control, and a node dispatched to §9 would find its stated measure green while the reason §9 exists (§1: every live reckon run reads `process_alive: null`) is still unfixed

findings.reason: the inference the figure supports (each run settles once, ~1.01 rows per distinct run, ~93 % `complete → recorded`) is confirmed by my counts at every window tried — the number is wrong and should be corrected or given its window, but the deduplication mechanism it argues for is right either way.
findings.text: §14 supports "A settle into `recorded` or `promoted` is one landing row per run" with "Measured over the reckon stream: 1,580 `→ recorded` rows across 1,559 runs, 1,452 of them `complete → recorded`", and that count does not reproduce from the file it names: over `~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.events` (98 MB, 2026-09-01T13:52Z to 2026-10-23T23:09Z) I count 3,337 `to_state: recorded` rows across 3,276 distinct runs, 3,120 of them `from_state: complete`, and over §1's own census window (48 h ending 2026-10-23T12:37Z) 390 rows across 388 runs, 354 from `complete` — no window of that stream yields 1,580, and the all-project population yields 7,174; my instrument does see recorded rows (the positive control), so this is the citation and not the parser

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol the two units cite resolves at HEAD: `watch_unit.live_foreign_seat` (:148), `live_foreign_seat_host` (:143), `_record_producer_running` (:91), `runs.watch_host_lease` (:2858) and `runs._seat_host_is_local` (:2794), `fleet_supervisor.RECORD_NAME` (`fleet_supervisor.py:108`), `dispatch_launch.py` about line 2128 (the fleet-record reader block at :2118-2135), `recovery_watch._watch_registration` (`recovery_watch.py:343`), and on §14's side `ticker.CARRIED_PANE_WORDS` (:360), `ticker._observer_exception` (:1514, called from `_feed` at :1820, ahead of the `stream_carries` filter in `feed` at :1606, so `_observer_exception` drops a settled row for a `_told` run, so §14's "changing only one of the two still drops the row" holds), `ticker._pane_word` (:1178), and `recovery_watch._watch_transition` (`recovery_watch.py:1885`, which writes `snapshot.get("run_id")` and `snapshot.get("node")` at :1916-1917 — the review run's own, exactly as §14 now states).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §9's Done-when at :305 measures only the decision node, which already exists at HEAD, and the wiring node added at :307 (the producer's start-up and its lease renewal) has no measure and no negative control at all.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §14 and §9 name no scratch or node-local path; both send their evidence to the run's gate log, and §9 sends it to "recorded in the gate log", which is the manifest's durable `test_logs` path, not a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — neither unit introduces a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into a symbol, file, or comment; the symbols named are existing ones, and the mechanism prose states mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the three mechanism checks hold for both units (the stated causes match the cited rows; the mechanisms produce their done-whens, with the draft's "carried once each" now correctly resting on both `_observer_exception` AND the `stream_carries` rule, verified to be independent gates; and both name their production callers, `_watch_registration` for §9's start-up and `_watch_transition` for §14's reviewed-run field), but §14's supporting census figure does not reproduce from the stream it names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9's two nodes each carry one goal (decide the release decision; call it from the producer) on disjoint write paths, and §14 carries one deliverable, the row policy plus the event field it reads.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §14's order line ("after §4, before §5 and §7, and after §9's wiring node, which also writes `recovery_watch.py`") now agrees with §9's own second-node write paths at :307 (`recovery_watch.py`, `runs.py`) and with followup f-alwh-002 at :341, which orders §14 before §5/§7 on `ticker.py` and puts §13 after §9's wiring node so the shared `runs.py` is not written concurrently.
